newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa prays for poor at Christmas mass.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa prays for poor at Christmas mass.

text.p: Mother Teresa, who returned home last week to continue recovering from heart surgery, led a Christmas holy mass at her Calcutta mission on Wednesday morning.
"She was there in the prayer hall the whole morning praying for the poorest of poor," a spokeswoman for her religious order Missionaries of Charity told Reuters by telephone.
She said the 86-year-old Nobel peace prize winner, advised by doctors to avoid crowds for fear of catching infection, retired to her room after spending nearly three hours in the prayer hall.
"She has now gone back to her room and is resting. She appears to be tired and you know she is not very strong after all these illness," the spokeswoman said.
The Roman Catholic missionary was expected to rest in her bed until evening prayer.

Earlier on Tuesday night, Mother Teresa led a Christmas mass at her mission. The mass was held four hours before the customary midnight mass to enable the revered nun to lead the 90-minute ceremony, aides said.
"Love one another as Jesus loves each one of you," the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner said in her message, delivered while seated.
Mother Teresa earlier watched a Nativity play staged by volunteers from all over the world at the courtyard of her mission and home.

Mother Teresa, known as the Saint of the Gutters for her devotion to the poor and dying, spent three weeks in hospital in August and September for heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia. Two weeks later, she fell off a chair and struck her head.
In November, she underwent an operation to unblock two coronary arteries, her third heart operation in five years.
She returned home last week after a long period of recovery delayed by bronchitis and irregular heartbeat.
